statement: For every field F, n >= 0, and function f:{0,1}^n -> F, M_f(x)=sum_{a in {0,1}^n} f(a) product_{i:a_i=1} x_i product_{i:a_i=0}(1-x_i) is multilinear, agrees with f on the Boolean cube, and is zero as a formal polynomial iff f is identically zero. Its displayed representation has at most 2^n terms and O(n*2^n) literal factors.
proof: At Boolean input b only the summand a=b survives, so M_f(b)=f(b); multilinearity is immediate. If a multilinear polynomial P vanishes on the cube, induct on n. Write P=A+x_n B with A,B multilinear. The restrictions x_n=0 and x_n=1 vanish on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=0 and A+B=0, hence B=0. Thus P=0. Applying this to M_f proves the equivalence. The displayed sum has 2^n terms of n factors each.

statement: Let R=Z[x_1,...,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i:1<=i<=n). For every polynomial P in Z[x_1,...,x_n], its class in R is zero iff P(a)=0 for every a in {0,1}^n. Consequently, for any CNF φ, the class of its literal-product satisfaction indicator P_φ=∏_j(1-∏_{literal occurrences ℓ in C_j}(1-ℓ)), where ℓ=x_i for a positive literal and ℓ=1-x_i for a negative literal, is zero in R iff φ is unsatisfiable. Proof: Modulo x_i^2=x_i, reduce each monomial by replacing every positive exponent of x_i by 1; this gives a multilinear representative with the same Boolean evaluations. A multilinear polynomial vanishing on the Boolean cube is the zero polynomial, by induction on n: write it A+x_nB; restrictions at x_n=0 and x_n=1 imply A=0 and A+B=0 on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=B=0. Thus P's class is zero exactly when all evaluations vanish. On Boolean inputs P_φ is 1 precisely when every clause has a true literal, hence it vanishes on the cube iff φ has no satisfying assignment.

statement: For every n>=0 and every multilinear polynomial Q(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} c_S product_{i in S} x_i over the integers, the Boolean-cube sum is sum_{a in {0,1}^n} Q(a)=sum_{S subseteq[n]} c_S 2^{n-|S|}. Consequently, if Q is the unique multilinear representative modulo (x_i^2-x_i) of a CNF satisfaction indicator, this weighted coefficient sum equals #SAT of that CNF. Proof: finite-sum interchange gives sum_a sum_S c_S product_{i in S}a_i = sum_S c_S sum_a product_{i in S}a_i. For fixed S, the monomial equals 1 iff all coordinates in S are 1; the remaining n-|S| coordinates are free, so exactly 2^{n-|S|} assignments contribute 1. The n=0 case uses S=empty and has one assignment. This is an identity over integers, not modulo a finite field, and asserts no efficient coefficient extraction from an arithmetic-circuit description.

statement: For every n≥0, d≥0, and multilinear Q(x)=Σ_{U⊆[n], |U|≤d} c_U x_U over Z, all coefficients c_S and the Boolean-cube sum Σ_a Q(a) can be recovered from the evaluations Q(1_T,0_[n]\T) for |T|≤d. Specifically, c_S=Σ_{T⊆S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}Q(1_T,0_[n]\T), and Σ_a Q(a)=Σ_{|S|≤d}2^{n-|S|}c_S. Therefore, given evaluation access to Q, the cube sum is computable using at most Σ_{j=0}^d binom(n,j) evaluations and O(3^d binom(n,d)) arithmetic operations (or O(d 2^d binom(n,d)) with straightforward subset accumulation), hence polynomially many evaluations and operations for fixed d. Proof: For each T, Q(1_T,0)=Σ_{U⊆T, |U|≤d}c_U. Möbius inversion on the subset lattice yields the displayed coefficient formula for each |S|≤d. The earlier monomial counting identity gives the cube sum. All queried T have size at most d. This is an exact procedure for bounded-degree multilinear representatives; it asserts no bounded-degree guarantee for general CNF indicators and no ordinary-PIT reduction.
